title: Local Frobenius polynomials
statement:
Keep the notation of [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence], so
that $(V,\rho)$ is the Weil fundamental representation of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], and let $x$ be a closed point of
$C_0$ of degree $e_x$, with local Frobenius $F_x$ of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] acting on the stalk
$\mathcal F_{\bar x}$; it acts through the conjugacy class of
geometric Frobenius elements at $x$ (images of the geometric Frobenius of
$k(x)$ under a decomposition-group map $\pi_1(x)\to\pi_1(C_0)$), of degree $e_x$, in the Weil group $W(C_0)$ of [def-wf-weil-group],
the geometric Frobenius over $k(x)$ having degree $e_x$ by
[lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension]. (Changing the decomposition-group
map conjugates $F_x$ by some $g\in\pi_1(C_0)$, and this is a conjugation
inside $W(C_0)$: as $\widehat{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z+e_x\widehat{\mathbf Z}$,
one can write $g=wF_x^t$ with $w\in W(C_0)$ and $t\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}$,
where $F_x^t$ is the image of the $t$-th power of the geometric Frobenius
in the procyclic group $\pi_1(x)$, which commutes with $F_x$; so
$gF_xg^{-1}=wF_xw^{-1}$.) Use the tensor equivalence
[prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] for the operations of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations] (direct sum, tensor product, dual,
exterior powers, determinant), and
write $P_x(\mathcal F,T)=\det(1-TF_x\mid\mathcal F_{\bar x})$ for the local
characteristic factor of [def-wf-iota-real]. Then

$$
P_x(\mathcal F,T)=\det\bigl(1-T\,\rho(F_x)\mid V\bigr)
\qquad\text{for every closed }x .
$$

proof.text: Work over a common finite coefficient field $E$. Indeed, [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] supplies a finite-field lisse model of the underlying $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf. In the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], represent $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ over a finite extension of that field. Their two inverse equations hold after a further finite extension, by the stated equality rule in the filtered Hom colimit. Hence these representatives give an actual $E$-Weil pair, with lisse underlying object; no integral lattice stable under $\theta$ is required. Apply [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] to this model: its pullbacks, fibres, and iterated point transports become those of an ordinary lisse module sheaf. By [d-real-setup] the geometric curve $C$ is connected, smooth, separated and finite type, so [lem-real-lisse-path-fibres] applies. Write $b=\bar\eta$, $V_E=\mathcal F_{E,b}$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{C_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, and $\theta:g^*\mathcal F_E\to\mathcal F_E$. All subsequent maps extend to the original coefficients by the scalar compatibilities in these cited statements.

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), (1.1.10); common-stage coefficient convention and the cited normalized realization

proof.text:
Use [lem-real-weil-twisted-paths] to identify $w\in W(C_0,b)$ of degree $n$ with a path $p_w:b\rightsquigarrow g^n b$. For $n\geq0$ let $\theta^{[0]}=1$ and $\theta^{[n]}=\theta\circ g^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ(g^{n-1})^*\theta$; define negative iterates using inverses. With pullback-stalk identifications understood, put $A_b(w)=\theta_b^{[n]}(p_w)_{\mathcal F_E}$. The path naturality and pullback rule of [lem-real-lisse-path-fibres] give
$$(p_w)_{\mathcal F_E}\theta_b^{[m]}=\theta_{g^n b}^{[m]}(g^m p_w)_{\mathcal F_E}.$$
Also $\theta_b^{[n]}\theta_{g^n b}^{[m]}=\theta_b^{[n+m]}$: for nonnegative exponents both sides are the same ordered list of factors; cancelling inverse factors gives the equality for integers. Combining these equations with the multiplication formula in the twisted-path lemma gives $A_b(w)A_b(v)=A_b(wv)$, and the zero iterate gives $A_b(1)=1$.

source.place: (1.1.10)-(1.1.12); explicit evaluation of the action on (X,F)

proof.text:
For degree zero, [lem-real-lisse-path-fibres] identifies $A_b(\delta)$ with $\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)$. Choose the degree-one lift $s$ used in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Its path is $p_s$, so the definition of its stalk transport and the descent operator is precisely $T_s=\theta_b(p_s)_{\mathcal F_E}=A_b(s)$. Every $w$ has the form $\delta s^n$, with $\delta=ws^{-n}$ in the geometric subgroup. The multiplication just checked therefore yields
$$A_b(w)=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)T_s^n=\rho(w),$$
where the last equality is the defining formula in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. This identifies the constructed action with the particular fundamental representation in the statement, rather than with an unspecified equivalent representation.

source.place: (1.1.12); comparison with the degree-one construction of def-wf-fundamental-representation

proof.text:
Fix a closed $x$ and its lift $a=\bar x$, put $e=e_x$, and choose a geometric path $\tau:a\rightsquigarrow b$ using [lem-real-lisse-path-fibres]. Let $u=\tau_{\mathcal F_E}:\mathcal F_{E,a}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_E$. In [lem-real-weil-twisted-paths] the decomposition Frobenius $f_x$ corresponds to the path $p_{f_x}=g^e(\tau)c_{a,e}\tau^{-1}$. Naturality of $\tau$ for the actual sheaf map $\theta^{[e]}:(g^e)^*\mathcal F_E\to\mathcal F_E$, and its pullback rule, give the explicit square
$$u\theta_a^{[e]}=\theta_b^{[e]}(g^e\tau)_{\mathcal F_E}.$$
Consequently the action computed in the preceding steps satisfies
$$\rho(f_x)=\theta_b^{[e]}(p_{f_x})_{\mathcal F_E}=u\bigl(\theta_a^{[e]}(c_{a,e})_{\mathcal F_E}\bigr)u^{-1}.$$
Thus $u$ intertwines the cyclic local Weil action (all integer powers of $f_x$) with the represented action. The underlying finite-etale paths also intertwine the full decomposition group by conjugation; for a general Weil sheaf only its integer-degree subgroup acts on the sheaf.

source.place: (1.1.8), (1.1.12)-(1.1.13); explicit naturality square at the closed point

proof.text: The remaining operator is exactly the framework local operator, as a map and with its normalization. Under [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], the source of the local composite in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is the ordinary fibre $\mathcal F_{E,a}$. Its first arrow $I_N^{[e]}$ is the iterated restriction-and-coprojection transport; its middle arrow identifies $g^e a=a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$. On finite locally constant sheaves this composite sends a lifted geometric point $z$ to $z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$, hence is $(c_{a,e})_{\mathcal F_E}$ by [lem-real-weil-twisted-paths]. The finite-level maps extend to integral models by their compatible inverse limits, then to rational maps and coefficient extensions by [lem-real-lisse-path-fibres]. The realization lemma identifies the framework iterates with these same ordinary transports. The last arrow is evaluation of $\theta^{[e]}$ at $a$. Therefore $F_x=\theta_a^{[e]}(c_{a,e})_{\mathcal F_E}$ on the degree-zero fibre. Substituting into the preceding displayed equation gives $uF_xu^{-1}=\rho(f_x)$ over $E$ and over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Second paragraph: expanded comparison of the specified local operator, using Deligne (1.1.7)-(1.1.8) and the normalized realization

proof.text: The degree of $f_x$ is $e_x$ by [lem-real-weil-twisted-paths], consistent with the normalization of [lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension]. A different arithmetic path changes $f_x$ to $h f_x h^{-1}$ for $h\in\pi_1(C_0,b)$. Write $\deg h=n+e_x t$, with $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $t\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}$; this is the elementary quotient calculation $\widehat{\mathbf Z}/e_x\widehat{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z/e_x\mathbf Z$. The image $f_x^t$ of the profinite power in $\pi_1(x)$ commutes with $f_x$. Thus $w=h f_x^{-t}$ has integer degree $n$, belongs to $W(C_0,b)$ by [def-wf-weil-group], and $h f_x h^{-1}=w f_x w^{-1}$. No value of $\rho$ on $f_x^t$ or on a general element of $\pi_1(C_0)$ is used. The stalk comparison therefore describes the required conjugacy class inside the Weil group.

The operations are transported through the exact tensor equivalence [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] using the actions specified in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. For the local polynomial use [def-wf-iota-real] and the established equation $uF_xu^{-1}=\rho(f_x)$. In a basis transported by $u$, the two operators have the same matrix; hence their determinants $\det(1-TF_x)$ and $\det(1-T\rho(f_x))$ are equal. Replacing $f_x$ by $w f_x w^{-1}$ replaces its matrix by conjugation by $\rho(w)$; multiplicativity of the determinant over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell[T]$ cancels the two inverse change-of-basis factors. This proves the asserted identity for every member of the Frobenius class, including rank zero, where both determinants are $1$.

source.place: Second paragraph: operations and final determinant equality

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs, expanded through finite coefficient models, natural lisse paths and coefficient-free twisted loops; Deligne Weil II (1.1.1), (1.1.7)-(1.1.13).

proof.text:
Changing the decomposition-group map conjugates $F_x$ by some
$g\in\pi_1(C_0)$, and this is a conjugation inside $W(C_0)$: as
$\widehat{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z+e_x\widehat{\mathbf Z}$, one can write
$g=wF_x^t$ with $w\in W(C_0)$ and $t\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}$, where $F_x^t$ is
the image of the $t$-th power of the geometric Frobenius in the procyclic
group $\pi_1(x)$, which commutes with $F_x$; so $gF_xg^{-1}=wF_xw^{-1}$.
Hence $F_x$ is well defined up to conjugacy in $W(C_0)$.

Granted [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence], the operations of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations] on
lisse Weil sheaves are *defined* by transport along the equivalence, so
only the local polynomial needs an argument. Iterating the Frobenius
structure map $e_x$ times on the stalk at $\bar x$, as in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], realizes $F_x$ as $\rho$ of
any member of the degree-$e_x$ class supplied by $x$. A characteristic
polynomial is invariant under conjugation, so $\det(1-T\rho(F_x)\mid V)$ is
independent of the member chosen and agrees with the stalkwise $P_x$ of [def-wf-iota-real].
